summary: Wave 9.1 — Automatic country / region detection. Backend: 8/8 wave9.1 tests pass on preview URL — GET /api/community/region/detect returns 200 with the full spec shape {ip, method, country, country_name, region, city, timezone, latitude, longitude, persisted, default_country}; method ∈ {ip,language,default,timezone}; default_country='CO'. X-Forwarded-For 190.85.107.5 → country=CO, city='Bogota', timezone='America/Bogota', method='ip'. X-Forwarded-For 189.203.229.65 → country=MX, method='ip'. Cache warm (2x same IP <5s) returns same payload. Authed member (member.demo) hit → persisted=true, /me returns country='CO'. After PATCH /me/region {country:'MX'} sets manual, subsequent /region/detect with CO IP → persisted=false and stored country stays MX (manual lock respected). Anon call → persisted=false, country still populated. Regional discovery still works: /api/discovery/trending?limit=8 with X-Region-Country: CO → first item has regional_weight=1.0; /api/discovery/entity/microsoft/related has CO within top-3 similar. Regression: 58/58 pass across test_wave8a_ecosystem + test_discovery + test_sources_center + test_growth + test_wave7_growth + test_wave6_auth_email. Frontend on fresh state (localStorage cleared): NO modal / no wizard prompts country selection on first visit; region chip resolves within <1s (well under the 8s spec bound) with a country name (not 'Detectando…'); data-testid='workspace-region-method' shows 'AUTO' when detection is auto (method != 'manual'); localStorage['pcone_country'] is written. Manual override: clicking chip → data-testid='workspace-region-option-CO' → label becomes 'Colombia', AUTO badge disappears; reload preserves Colombia + storage='CO' + no AUTO badge. Responsive: no horizontal scroll at 360/414/768/1440. Note: since Playwright runs from a US-egress datacenter, backend correctly detected 'Estados Unidos' as the initial auto country for the browser session (not CO) — the detection chain works; the country returned is a function of the client IP, which is expected.

ui_bugs.issue: workspace-region-chip is present in DOM but NOT visible on mobile/tablet viewports (360/414/768). Same as iteration_23 — ProfileCardWidget lives in the desktop-only workspace sidebar on the anon Home. Users on phones cannot see the AUTO badge or reach the picker via UI. Backend regionalization via X-Region-Country still applies once localStorage is seeded.

action_items: Consider exposing the region chip on mobile/tablet (mirror inside mobile top-nav or bottom-nav 'Mi Espacio' pane). Backend already regionalizes; any UI entry point is sufficient. This is carried over from iteration_23 — not a Wave 9.1 regression.
critical_code_review_comments: community_stats_routes.region_detect: IP extraction chain (cf-connecting-ip → x-real-ip → x-forwarded-for) is correct and proxy-safe; drops loopback IPs before hitting ipapi.co — good.

In-memory _region_cache (6h TTL) is process-local — behind multiple gunicorn workers each will hold its own cache. Acceptable given ipapi.co free tier of ~1000/day/IP, but if scaled horizontally consider Redis. Not a Wave 9.1 blocker.
region_detect persistence branch respects country_source=='manual' — the CENTRAL Wave 9.1 spec bullet — verified via test_persist_ip_then_manual_locks.

CommunityUserPublic schema does NOT expose country_source. This is fine for the frontend chip logic (useUserRegion derives method locally when detectedMethod is set), but means external API consumers can't see whether a user's country was auto or manual. Consider adding country_source: Optional[str] to CommunityUserPublic so the chip's AUTO badge stays accurate across page reloads for authed users too (currently after reload the badge relies on detectedMethod state which is null on remount when user.country already exists → chip won't render AUTO for authed users after refresh).

useUserRegion: after full reload for an authed user whose country was IP-persisted, the hook skips the detect call (localCountry from storage OR user.country short-circuits the effect). Method is then user.country_source — but /me does not return country_source, so `region.method` falls back to null and the AUTO badge disappears. If the intent is 'AUTO badge remains visible until user manually picks', wiring country_source through CommunityUserPublic would fix this.

Frontend detectFromBackend does not send a User-Agent-like tag and depends on backend for IP; when Playwright's egress is US, backend returns US which then becomes the visible label. This is by design.

Spec lists 'timezone' as an allowed method value; backend never emits it (only ip/language/default). Frontend hook emits 'timezone' when Intl-based fallback fires. Consistency is fine because the frontend derives method locally. Consider also emitting method='timezone' from the backend when the timezone header (if any) is used — currently backend has no timezone fallback path; not a blocker.

success_rate.frontend: 10/11 spec assertions pass; the pre-existing mobile-chip visibility carries over from Wave 9

test_credentials: member.demo@puntocero.test-e2e.com / MemberDemo2026 (verified). Test may temporarily unset user.country_source via direct MongoDB write to validate the auto→manual→lock cycle; test restores country='CO' at end.
seed_data_creation: None (test uses PATCH /me/region + a direct DB $unset of country_source for setup, then restores).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Wave 9.1 backend endpoint /api/community/region/detect works exactly per spec. Reusable test at /app/backend/tests/test_wave9_1_region_detect.py (8 tests). ipapi.co is reachable from the preview backend and returns CO/MX data for known IPs. Two watch-outs for anyone iterating on this: (1) CommunityUserPublic doesn't return country_source, so the AUTO badge only survives across page reloads for anon users (relies on localStorage + detectedMethod state), not authed users; (2) the manual-lock test defensively unsets country_source in MongoDB — running pytest requires MONGO_URL reachable (it is, mongodb://localhost:27017). Frontend chip remains desktop-only on mobile widths (iteration_23 finding still holds, not a Wave 9.1 regression).
rca of the issue: Not applicable — all Wave 9.1 spec assertions passed. The only carry-over UI observation (mobile chip invisibility) originates from ProfileCardWidget being rendered only in the desktop workspace sidebar layout, unrelated to Wave 9.1.
